# Which files does Codex CLI read?

Driftgate adapter id: `codex` · Verified against CLI docs as published 2026-09-02 on 2026-09-02 · [Homepage](https://developers.openai.com/codex)

Every file below that is present is **sent to the model**, all together. The order ranks specificity rather than authority — nothing here overrides anything else.

## Precedence

| # | Path | Scope | Role | Driftgate writes it | Nesting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AGENTS.override.md` | nested | instructions | no | nearest-wins |
| 2 | `AGENTS.md` | project | instructions | yes | nearest-wins |
| 3 | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | user-level | instructions | no | root only |
| 4 | `.codex/config.toml` | project | mcp | yes | root only |
| 5 | `~/.codex/config.toml` | user-level | settings | no | root only |

## What each file is

### `AGENTS.override.md`

Checked before AGENTS.md at every level from the git root down. Never generated by Driftgate: its purpose is to override the shared file, so writing it would defeat it.

Source: [Codex — Custom instructions with AGENTS.md](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) — retrieved 2026-09-02

### `AGENTS.md`

The file Driftgate generates. Codex walks from the git root to the working directory collecting one of these per level and concatenates them, so a nested AGENTS.md adds to the root file rather than replacing it — and, being later in the prompt, wins where they conflict.

Source: [Codex — Custom instructions with AGENTS.md](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) — retrieved 2026-09-02

### `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`

User-level instructions applied to every project, read before any repository file. Read-only context for `doctor`: Driftgate never writes outside the repository.

Source: [Codex — Custom instructions with AGENTS.md](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) — retrieved 2026-09-02

### `.codex/config.toml`

Project-level Codex settings, loaded only for a project the user has trusted. Driftgate generates this file from `.driftgate/mcp/servers.yaml` and owns it in full — unlike the other MCP targets, it is not an MCP-only file.

Source: [Codex — Config reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) — retrieved 2026-09-04

### `~/.codex/config.toml`

Codex settings. Two keys change what this adapter’s output means: `project_doc_max_bytes` (32 KiB default) caps the combined instruction text, and `project_doc_fallback_filenames` adds further filenames Codex will accept in place of AGENTS.md.

Source: [Codex — Custom instructions with AGENTS.md](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) — retrieved 2026-09-02

## Size limits

- Total: 32768 bytes

Codex stops adding instruction files once the concatenated text reaches `project_doc_max_bytes`, 32 KiB by default. Files are added root-first, so it is the nearest — most specific — file that gets dropped when the budget runs out.

## Notes

- **warn** — A server Codex cannot express is omitted from .codex/config.toml and named in it as a `# omitted:` comment, rather than failing the run (T083). Codex resolves environment references only through env_vars (which needs the variable and the key to share a name) and bearer_token_env_var (Authorization only), so a renamed reference or a credential in another header has nowhere to go. Check the top of the generated file if a server you configured is missing.
  Source: [Codex — Extend with MCP servers](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) — retrieved 2026-09-04
- **warn** — Driftgate owns the whole of `.codex/config.toml`, not just its `[mcp_servers.*]` tables — it is where every Codex setting lives, and there is no way to write part of a file. A pre-existing one is somebody else’s and is refused until `--force` backs it up; a setting added by hand afterwards is reported as a hand-edit that `sync --import` can recover.
  Source: [Codex — Config reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) — retrieved 2026-09-04
- **warn** — Codex has no variable substitution anywhere in config.toml, so an `env:NAME` reference cannot be written as a value the way `${NAME}` and `${env:NAME}` are elsewhere — it has to become a different key. `env: { NAME: env:NAME }` becomes `env_vars = ["NAME"]`, and an Authorization header becomes `bearer_token_env_var`. A reference those two keys cannot express — a renamed variable, or any other header — is refused rather than dropped: a credential that never arrives is a server that starts and fails to authenticate.
  Source: [Codex — Extend with MCP servers](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) — retrieved 2026-09-04
- **warn** — Codex documents streamable HTTP only, with no discriminator for SSE, so a canonical `transport: sse` renders as a bare `url` and the distinction is lost. Lossy but still a working server — the same treatment Cursor’s missing `type` key gets, and the reason it is recorded here rather than left for a user to find.
  Source: [Codex — Extend with MCP servers](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) — retrieved 2026-09-04
- **warn** — AGENTS.md is both a canonical *input* Driftgate accepts and this adapter’s *output*. When a repository has no `.driftgate/` and is using AGENTS.md as its canonical source, this adapter emits nothing rather than generating the file from itself.
  Source: [AGENTS.md — a simple, open format for guiding coding agents](https://agents.md/) — retrieved 2026-09-02
- **info** — AGENTS.md is a cross-vendor format, not a Codex format: VS Code, Cursor, Copilot, Jules, Zed and others read it too. Enabling this adapter alongside claude-code or gemini therefore hands some tools the same rules twice, from two files. That is not an error, but it is worth knowing before it shows up as a doubled token count.
  Source: [AGENTS.md — a simple, open format for guiding coding agents](https://agents.md/) — retrieved 2026-09-02
- **info** — Codex has no per-glob rule mechanism, so a glob-scoped canonical rule is rendered with an "Applies to:" line stating its scope in prose. Lossy, but visibly so; dropping the scope silently would turn a component-only rule into a repo-wide one.
